title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City School Board met Thursday evening, delayed by one week to meet the legal requirements for adopting the annual budget.  To satisfy that need, they began with the FY2026 Budget hearing.  It was short-lived, as no visitors were on hand so the hearing adjourned and the regular meeting got underway.

Chairman Misty Lindeman called the meeting to order and the board quickly approved the board agenda, past meeting minutes and moved on to approve the Financial Report.  Superintendent John Neubaum highlighted a couple of points.  He stated Clay City Schools ended the year a little out, but they were within their target.  He also spoke briefly about Tort issues but there were no major issues.  He said the district closed out the year with routine bills except for the sports co-op agreement with North Clay.  There were a couple of questions about unrelated fees paid to Clay County Hospital and Blue Cross Blue Shield, however Supt. Neubaum was able to quickly explain both issues and the meeting continued.

In informational items, the Supt. Stated the district finished the school year with 202 students enrolled and said the numbers for next year are hard to pin down, due to the ebb and flow of students in to and out of the district.  Neubaum also spent a moment on the continuing issue of FOIA (Freedom of Information Act) requests.  The district received five inquiries that once a response is issued, they then transform into commercial opportunities.  Before moving on, Supt. Neubaum updated the board on summer maintenance and repairs.  Cleaning efforts are ongoing and they are ready for the installation of a new air conditioner on the roof but are waiting for a crane to be available to lift the units.  Concerning that project, he said a vendor, Veragy Solutions, suggested installing the unit on the ground rather than the roof to prevent leaks and they suggested separating the outside air intake and the exhaust outlet for a more efficient HVAC system.

Principal Brian Wattles presented his report and noted that summer school is winding down.  Clay City FFA members attended FFA meeting in Springfield and participated in the election of officers.  He adds that student LouEllen Harvel in the Drumline.  The FFA Alumni Dinner is June 26.  Wattles also reported on the success of the North Clay/Clay City Baseball Team capturing Third Place in the IHSA Class A State Tournament and he noted the inclusion Clay City students Cayden Craig and Chase Bangert on that outstanding team.  He also reported on the student trip to Europe and called on Teacher Candace Walker to speak briefly about the trip.  Walker indicated the trip left St. Louis on June 2 and returned on the 12th.  Their trip included a stopover in Canada and then they visited Dublin, Ireland; Cardiff, Wales; London, England; and Paris, France.  Walker said they saw and experienced so many wonderful things.  On the way back, they stopped in Toronto and then travelled on to St. Louis but were forced to return to Canada due stormy weather and had to spend an extra night away causing concern by anxious parents.  But all ended well and they enjoyed their trip.

In New Business, the board approved many items in quick succession.  It started with Ted Whitehead with Snedeker Risk Management presenting the Commercial Insurance Fees for FY2027.  As Supt. Neubaum introduced Whitehead he noted that the district’s valuation has risen from $26.77 Million to $31.37 Million.  Whithead noted that with that increase, he noted that insurance fees were up as well, by roughly $12,000.  Members approved the measure unanimously.  Next, the board approved an Inter-Governmental Agreement with Flora Public Library to permit students to use the library.  They also approved the Board Policy Manual.  Members then approved the FY2026 Amended Budget and went on to agree on the Certified and Non-Certified Staff Attendance Bonus List for the second semester.  The board then approved the Non-Certified Employee Handbook.  Next there was a fairly lengthy conversation about the student handbook for the next school year.  Specifically, it concerned creating a district policy that will regulate students’ use of electronic devices during instructional time, with limited exceptions such as medical needs. Illinois Schools will be required to develop a policy by the 2027-28 school year.  The board voted to adopt the student handbook as presented with the policy potentially altered at future meetings.  The measure passed on a 4-2 vote, with Mary Jo Patridge, Amanda Noll, Mary Jo Workman and Oliver Bangert voting Yes and Misty Lindeman and Dusty Thompson voting No.

Before adjourning, the board approved several personnel actions.  Brady Martin was approved as Summer Help; Megan Hildebrand was approved as Student Council and National Honor Society Sponsor; Candace Walker was approved as High School Scholastic Bowl Coach; Gina Hutton approved as High School JV Scholastic Bowl Coach; Beth Hance as Jr. High Volleyball Coach; Ashtyn Goldman approved as Jr. High Assistant Volleyball Coach and Jr. High Assistant Cross Country Coach; Jess Hosselton approved as FFA Sponsor and Senior Class Sponsor; Pam Garrison approved as Junor Class Sponsor; Courtney Mitchel approved as Athletic Director, Jr. High Head Cross Country Coach, Jr. High Head Track and Field Coach, High School Assistant Cross Country Coach and Junor Class Sponsor; Jacob Martin approved as High School Head Cross Country Coach; and Nathan Deain approved as Jr. High Assistant Track Coach.  The final action of the meeting was board approval to open an Activity Account for the Class of 2030.  With all business concluded, the meeting adjourned.

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
Noble trustees approved a fiscal appropriations ordinance on Monday night, with projected expenditures exceeding estimated revenues by more than $719,000, at nearly $1.57 million.  The appropriations ordinance listed revenues of $850,565 for the fiscal year beginning May 1st, while expenditures were projected at over $1.56 million.

Trustees then passed a motion allowing Ameren Illinois to construct and operate an electric utility system within the village.  The measure passed unanimously extending authorization to the power company.  Village engineer Brandon Bridges said he posted notice for the village’s Motor Fuel Tax bid opening scheduled for July 1st at 10 am.  The bids will cover roadway work on the north and south roads and will be opened at Noble Village Hall.

The board continued the evening’s discussion regarding nuisance properties with non-compliant lawns.  Notices have already been sent to property owners, and trustees directed follow up notices be sent to those still out of compliance and warned corrective costs may follow.

The upcoming Freedom Festival and Parade at Noble Park was highlighted with activities scheduled for Saturday, June 27, beginning at 9 am.

Activities will include craft and flea market vendors from 9 am to 2 pm, a tractor, lawn mower and car display from 9 am to noon, children’s activities and live music from 11 am to 2 pm.  Food vendors will include Smokin’ Pig and Wetherell Concessions, and the Noble Lions Club will provide free watermelon from 11 am to 2 pm.  The parade begins at 1 pm and is expected to feature more than 100 entries this year.

title: JULY BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
ImpactLife will have a blood drive on Wednesday at the Iuka Fire Protection District from 4 to 7 pm.  Then there will be another blood drive at the Clay County Hospital on Thursday, July 9th from 10 am to 1 pm.  To schedule an appointment at either of these drives go to https://login.bloodcenter.org/donor/schedules/drive_schedule/144076

The American Red Cross is also making an urgent call for blood donors to book an appointment to give now to ensure hospitals stay ready to help patients without delay.

There will be a blood drive Friday, July 10th from 1 to 5 pm at the Clay County Health Department.  All donors who donate blood during this drive will get a American Red Cross Looney Tunes T-shirt.  Then there will be a Blood Drive at the Flora Oddfellows Lodge on Friday July 24th from 1 to 5 pm.  Donors at this drive will get a Fandango Movie Reward by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  You can make an appointment to donate at Red Cross Blood Drives by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  Save time with RapidPass.  Complete your pre-donation reading and health history at RedCrossBlood.org/RapidPass or with the Blood Donor App before your appointment.

title: WAYNE COUNTY SHERIFF’S GRANT
full_story:
The Illinois Counties Risk Management Trust (ICRMT) awarded a Safety Grant to the Wayne County Sheriff’s Office on a recent technology upgrade within their facility that focuses on inmate safety.

This improvement will assist Correctional Officers by remotely measuring health metrics using FDA approved technology that can rapidly notify staff of any potential medical distress being experienced by persons in-custody.  The equipment has been installed and is currently being utilized by Correctional Staff within the Wayne County Jail.

title: CENTRALIA WOMAN STEALS CAR
full_story:
A 69-year-old Centralia woman had her pretrial release revoked after new charges were filed against her for allegedly walking out of the Marion County Courthouse Monday and stealing a vehicle.

Judge Ericka Sanders released Joyce King of Centralia on pre-trial conditions after her first appearance for aggravated battery to a nurse and criminal trespass to property on Monday.  Her new charges are unlawful possession of a stolen or converted vehicle and theft.

The vehicle and King were later found at a restaurant in Mt. Vernon.  Salem Police say the keys to the vehicle were left inside the vehicle.

King was ordered to remain in custody after her Wednesday court appearance.  She was also ordered to undergo a fitness exam.

title: INTRODUCTION TO NURSING
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting an Introduction to Nursing event for high school students on Tuesday, July 14th from 10 am to 4 pm in Neal Hall room 101.  The event is designed for students interested in the nursing profession to learn about the programs and resources available at Lake Land College as well as the career opportunities available in the field.

During the event, students in attendance will meet with faculty and staff, tour Lake Land’s nursing facilities and develop their skills in a variety of hands-on activities.  They will also enjoy the opportunity to experience and practice realistic patient care in the College’s high-fidelity patient simulation lab.  Additionally, attendees will learn everything they need to know about the nursing program admission process, from financial aid options to tips for the entrance exam.  A free pizza lunch will also be provided for all students in attendance.

Space for the Introduction to Nursing event is limited to the first 30 registrants.  Registration is available online.

The Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event is offered with sponsorship support from St. Anthony’s Memorial Hospital and Good Shepard Hospital.

To learn more about the Lake Land College Introduction to Nursing Event, contact Nursing Instructor Nichole Jones at 217-234-5455 or [email protected].

title: IDPH LEAD SCREENINGS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Public Health said universal childhood blood lead testing will begin Wednesday, expanding testing to all children statewide.

The blood testing will be done automatically at 12 and 24 months.  Healthcare providers will also be required to assess all children six years old and younger for lead exposure with a questionnaire.

The Illinois Department of Public Health said the change is the culmination of a years-long effort to expand the number of children who are tested.  Officials said childhood testing leads to earlier intervention, which means better outcomes for impacted children.

“There is no safe level of lead in the blood,” IDPH Director Dr. Sameer Vohra said in a news release.  “Through our Childhood Lead Program, IDPH has identified thousands of children who have been exposed to lead, allowing for early intervention to address negative health effects and implementation of efforts to limit further exposure.  With this move to universal childhood blood lead testing, IDPH is taking another step towards protecting the health and safety of Illinois’ youngest residents.”

If a child’s blood test comes back showing lead levels more than 3.5 micrograms per deciliter, a public health intervention will be required.  This means a health inspector would work to determine the source of the lead contamination.  If lead is found in the home, the inspector would work with the resident to remove it.  A public health nurse would also educate the family on how to protect children from lead exposure.

Lead exposure can cause developmental, behavioral and learning difficulties.  You can learn more information about lead exposure online by visiting the IDPH’s website.

title: AMERICA 250
full_story:
Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias is inviting Illinoisans to celebrate America’s 250th anniversary with the launch of a new America 250 website, Illinois State Archives social media channels and a series of exhibitions and events highlighting Illinois’ profound impact on the nation’s history.

Beginning in July, residents can participate in a public reading of the Declaration of Independence, explore a new archival exhibit and enjoy free, family‑friendly activities across Springfield’s Capitol Complex.

“Illinois has helped shape the American story from the frontier days of Abraham Lincoln to the innovations, movements and leaders that continue to influence our nation today,” said Giannoulias, who also serves as the State Archivist and State Librarian.  “As we commemorate this historic milestone, we invite Illinoisans to discover the people, places and moments that helped define our state and country.  This is an opportunity to reflect on where we’ve been, celebrate how far we’ve come and inspire future generations to carry those ideals and values forward.”

The new America 250 webpage serves as a digital gateway to Illinois history, showcasing the state’s contributions to the nation’s political, economic, agricultural and cultural development.  Visitors can explore historic photographs, documents and other treasures from the collections of the Illinois State Archives and the Illinois State Library while also accessing a complete schedule of America 250 events and activities taking place throughout the Capitol Complex.

As part of the America 250 commemoration, the Illinois State Archives has launched official social media channels – @ilstatearchives – to help bring Illinois history to new audiences and engage residents in the celebration leading up to the nation’s 250th anniversary.  Through historical photographs, documents, artifacts and behind-the-scenes content, the channels showcase the stories, people and events that shaped Illinois and the nation.

On July 8th, Illinois will join all 50 states in a simultaneous public reading of the Declaration of Independence.  The event will begin at 5 pm on the steps of the Illinois State Capitol and is open to the public.

On July 9th, the State Archives and State Library will debut “America 250: Land of Lincoln,” a summer-long exhibition celebrating Illinois’ place in the nation’s history.  The exhibit features historic plat maps from across the state, original surveyors’ notes and land records connected to Abraham Lincoln, offering visitors a rare glimpse into the people, communities and landscapes that shaped Illinois history.  This exhibit will remain on display through Labor Day.

The celebration continues July 17th and 18th with a free, two-day family event hosted in partnership with the Illinois State Museum and the Illinois Supreme Court.  Families can enjoy presentations from acclaimed Illinois children’s authors, archival conservation demonstrations, an American eagle flight demonstration, a Route 66 exhibit and other interactive experiences for visitors of all ages.

The event also provides a unique opportunity to explore the many educational and cultural resources available year-round at the Illinois State Capitol, Illinois State Archives, Illinois State Library, Illinois State Museum and Illinois Supreme Court Learning Center.  Activities will take place from 10 am to 4 pm throughout the Capitol Complex.

Follow the Illinois State Archives on social media at @ilstatearchives and view the full schedule of America 250 events at www.ilsos.gov/america250.
